title: Evidence Maturity Model and Orchestration Handbook
author: Anika Patel
content:
Overview:

This handbook defines Redwood's Evidence Maturity Model (EMM) and the operational orchestration patterns we use to ensure audit-ready control artifacts across RBAC & authorization, audit logging, data residency & retention, Secure SDLC gates, and incident response. It explains who owns each class of evidence, the lifecycle stages, retrieval/packaging SLAs, and the standard procedures to capture and preserve proof during incidents and audits.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: provide a single playbook to raise evidence readiness and automate packaging for internal reviews and external audits (SOC/ISO/GDPR).
- Scope: applies to production services, customer-dedicated deployments (Dedicated/Private), control exceptions, and model-serving artifacts. Does not replace legal counsel for cross-border holds.

Audience:

- Security engineers, compliance leads, SREs, platform engineers, product owners, and solutions engineers responsible for customer deployments.

Key definitions:

- Evidence: concrete artifact that demonstrates control enforcement (logs, attestation records, manifests, config snapshots, signed release artifacts).
- Proof manifest: compact JSON/YAML index describing a packaged evidence set (see Appendix A).
- Evidence guardian: the team or service responsible for retention, retrieval, and tamper-evident packaging for a given artifact type.

Evidence Maturity Model (EMM) Levels:

Level 0 — Ad hoc
- Evidence exists inconsistently or manually compiled; no automated retention or retrieval workflows.

Level 1 — Logged
- Event and config artifacts are produced but retention and packaging are manual. Basic retention policies configured.

Level 2 — Indexed
- Artifacts are indexed with stable identifiers and tags (tenant-id, model-id, control-id). Retrieval scripts exist and retrieval SLAs are measured.

Level 3 — Orchestrated
- Evidence guardians publish manifests and API endpoints for retrieval. Packaging and redaction are automated for routine audits. Access and chain-of-custody metadata included.

Level 4 — Certified
- Evidence sets are integrated with policy engines and can be produced as verifiable bundles (signed manifests, cryptographic hashes, provenance attestations). Business owners can self-serve attestations.

Mapping examples (control areas -> exemplar artifacts -> target EMM level):

| Control area | Exemplar artifacts | Target level |
|--------------|--------------------|--------------|
| RBAC & auth | role bindings export, privilege change logs, approval records | Level 3 |
| Audit logging | immutable log segments, indexing metadata, checksum proofs | Level 3-4 |
| Data residency & retention | geo-tagged storage manifests, retention policy snapshots | Level 3 |
| Secure SDLC | signed build artifacts, release gate approvals, dependency SBOM | Level 4 |
| Incident response | preserved telemetry bundle, legal-hold markers, chain-of-custody notes | Level 3 |

Operational ownership matrix:

- Example table (artifact type -> evidence guardian -> retention -> retrieval SLA -> owner contact):

| Artifact type | Evidence guardian | Min retention | Retrieval SLA | Owner |
|---------------|-------------------|---------------|---------------|-------|
| Access logs (prod API) | observability-team | 13 months | 2 hours | eng-sre@redwood.com |
| Role attestation records | identity-team | 36 months | 24 hours | security-id@redwood.com |
| Model artifact SBOM | build-platform | 7 years | 3 business days | eng-platform@redwood.com |
| Encrypted key custody records | crypto-ops | 7 years | 24 hours | security-ops@redwood.com |

Standard procedures:

1) Onboarding a new evidence type into EMM
- Step 1: Service owner opens an evidence intake ticket (label: evidence-intake) documenting artifact format, retention, tags, and initial retention store.
- Step 2: Identity and Observability teams verify that artifacts can be produced with required tags (tenant-id, region, control-id).
- Step 3: Evidence guardian implements indexing and publishes a retrieval endpoint (/evidence/v1/manifest/<artifact-id>).
- Step 4: Run compliance smoke-test: retrieve a sample manifest, validate tags, and confirm packaging pipeline can redact PII per data residency.

2) Incident evidence capture (fast path)
- Trigger conditions: any P1/P0 security incident or a legal hold.
- Actions (ordered):
  1. Declare legal hold if required and notify Legal@redwood.com.
  2. Evidence guardians run the preservation script: 
     CLI example: redwood-preserve --service payments --since "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z" --to /preserve/INC-1234 --tags "incident,tenant:acme"
  3. Add chain-of-custody entries to the manifest (actor, timestamp, method).
  4. Seal the bundle: compute SHA256 checksums for each file and sign the manifest with KMS key id=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/evidence/cryptoKeys/evidence-signing-key.
  5. Notify auditors and legal with the sealed bundle location and retrieval token.

Chain-of-custody minimum fields (must be included in every preserved manifest):
- event_id
- actor (email/service)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- preservation_method (CLI/API)
- preserving_guardian (team)
- integrity_hash (SHA256)

Guidelines for cross-border data residency and redaction:

- Before packaging, evidence guardians must consult the residency map to determine which artifacts require local redaction. If an artifact contains EU-personal-data and the bundle will be transferred to a non-EU auditor, apply the EU-redaction profile.
- Use the redaction pipeline: redwood-redact --manifest manifest.json --profile eu_personal_data --output redacted-bundle/
- Document redactions in the manifest with redaction_reason and redaction_script_version.

Audit packaging and submission checklist:

- [ ] Evidence manifest present and signed
- [ ] Chain-of-custody entries for all preserved artifacts
- [ ] Retention policy snapshot included and validated against current policy ID
- [ ] Redaction summary included (if redaction applied)
- [ ] Integrity checksums present for all files
- [ ] Access control policy snapshot (RBAC bindings) included
- [ ] Contact list for evidence guardians and legal liaison included

Proof manifest sample (stringified JSON example for auditors):

{
  "manifest_id": "manifest-2026-08-01-INC1234",
  "service": "payments",
  "preserved_by": "observability-team",
  "preserved_at": "2026-08-01T12:06:00Z",
  "files": ["api-access-logs-2026-07-31.gz", "role-changes-2026-07-30.csv"],
  "signatures": ["kms://evidence-signing-key#sig-1"],
  "chain_of_custody": ["see chain-of-custody log file: coc-INC1234.log"]
}
(When producing an external audit bundle, provide both original and redacted manifests and clearly mark the redaction policy applied.)

RBAC attestation cadence and automation:

- Attestation window: quarterly for business-critical roles; semi-annually for infra roles; yearly for low-risk service roles.
- Automation: identity-team runs an attestation job that produces an attestation artifact with schema: role_id, members_current, last_attested, approver.
- Required evidence for attestation: role-binding exports (CSV), approval ticket link, SSO signin logs (to correlate membership).

SLOs and metrics for evidence readiness:

- Evidence completeness (critical controls) >= 95% within 48 hours of onboarding event.
- Evidence retrieval SLA: 95th percentile <= 4 hours for incident bundles, <= 72 hours for audit-level bundles.
- Packaging integrity: 100% of manifests must include SHA256 checksums and chain-of-custody metadata.

Exception handling and risk acceptance:

- Control exceptions that affect evidence generation must go through the normal exception process. Documentation must include: compensating controls, evidence gaps, mitigation timeline, and acceptance by risk committee.
- Temporary access exceptions that impact logging or attestation require immediate compensating evidence (e.g., session recordings, elevated monitoring) and a post-change attestation within 7 days.

Operational runbook snippets:

- Preserve recent logs for an incident (fast command):
  redwood-preserve --service <svc> --since "<ISO>" --limit 500G --tags "incident,urgent" --output /preserve/INC-<id>

- Generate an evidence manifest from index (example):
  redwood-evidence-manifest create --index /indices/service-logs --filter "tenant:acme AND severity:warn..critical" --out manifest.json

- Seal manifest with KMS (example):
  gcloud kms keys versions sign --key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/evidence/cryptoKeys/evidence-signing-key --input-file=manifest.json --output-file=manifest.sig

Roadmap and next steps:

- Q3 2026: pilot Level 4 certified manifests for model-serving pipeline (SBOM + provenance).
- Q4 2026: automate cross-border redaction hooks in preservation pipeline.
- Q1 2027: integrate evidence manifest retrieval APIs with the compliance console and provide per-tenant audit bundles.

Ownership and escalation contacts:

- Evidence governance: security-compliance@redwood.com
- Observability/Evidence guardians: observability-team@redwood.com
- Identity & RBAC: identity-team@redwood.com
- Legal liaison (audit holds): legal@redwood.com

Appendix A — Evidence tag taxonomy (required tags):

- tenant_id
- service
- artifact_type
- region
- control_id
- retention_policy_id
- incident_id (optional)

Appendix B — Minimal manifest validation checklist (automation rules):

- manifest_id must be present and unique
- preserved_at must be ISO8601 and <= now
- files must be listed and checksums present
- chain_of_custody must reference at least one preserving_guardian

Appendix C — Legal hold quicknote:

If Legal issues a hold, the security on-call must annotate the evidence index with hold=true and freeze deletions. Notify the relevant evidence guardian teams immediately and escalate to the VP Security if cross-border transfer will be requested.
